context: Powerhouse continuity already requires current-state-first, delta-only, interruption recovery and safe parallel verification. The remaining gap was a reusable execution envelope that operationalizes these rules with task classes, bounded context, freshness-aware evidence reuse, candidate identity, parallel read-only retrieval and latency instrumentation.
root_cause: Latency controls existed as policy concepts but were not exposed through a canonical reusable runtime primitive and mandatory shared preflight metadata. During delivery, the first classifier implementation also treated the noun 'deploy' inside a read-only status/readback request as a mutating action, producing STANDARD instead of FAST.
decision: Add POWERHOUSE-FAST-EXECUTION-v1 as an optimization projection on the existing canonical Brain, never as a second memory, queue, orchestrator or truth store. Read-only intent wins over ambiguous operation nouns unless an actual mutation verb is present.

production_evidence.main_policy_readback: config/powerhouse-fast-execution-v1.json is ACTIVE and default_enabled=true on main
production_evidence.main_preflight_readback: scripts/brain/chat-learning-preflight.mjs includes the fast policy as mandatory supplemental source, fail-closes unless ACTIVE/default-enabled, verifies the runtime entrypoint exists, and exposes fastExecution metadata
gates_green: Unified BRAIN delivery including backend/portal/website/automation lanes
production_evidence.classifier_regression: BRAIN backend failure on the first candidate proved the ambiguous deploy classification bug; exact-head candidate a8bccc4c538b10a9ca7d841ef5c62960571c97ac passed BRAIN backend after the intent-aware fix.

prevention: All material agents and chats obtain the default fast-execution policy through the existing mandatory chat-learning preflight. Performance work may bound, cache, reuse and parallelize canonical reads, but may not bypass required direct observation, candidate identity, security, truth, release, interruption recovery, production readback or learning gates. Classification regressions must test both read-only inspection of a deploy and actual mutating deploy/update intent.
success_evidence: read-only deploy/status checks classify FAST while mutating deploy/update tasks remain STANDARD
context and tool output are bounded
expired, unbound or candidate-mismatched release evidence is rejected
mandatory preflight fail-closes unless fast-execution policy is ACTIVE and default-enabled
mandatory preflight exposes fastExecution metadata to every material agent/chat entrypoint
protected main contains the active policy and mandatory preflight integration
